trust_decision.summary: Whether a tenant/admin-supplied outbound URL (action target, actions-v1 fetch, IdP endpoints, SAML metadata, notification webhooks, back-channel logout URI) may be contacted is decided by a denylist check that at the pinned commit runs once before the request (pre-resolve check, then an unprotected client re-resolves and follows redirects), and only on some routes; the fix moves the decision into a shared client whose dialer Control hook and CheckRedirect enforce the denylist on every connection.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'denylist bypass in outgoing HTTP components'; the only runtime denylist check for Actions v2 targets is this pre-call IsHostBlocked followed by http.DefaultClient at internal/execution/execution.go:264, with the shared check in internal/denylist/host_checker.go:52.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Domain verification (internal/api/http/domain_check.go:35) must by design reach the org's own public website, is a pre-existing feature unrelated to actions/IdP/notifications, and the report is about 'denylist bypass', not a route that never had a denylist.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Sonyflake machine-ID lookup intentionally calls a configured cloud-metadata webhook (often 169.254.169.254) with a bare client; an over-broad fix that globally replaces http.DefaultTransport/DefaultClient with the denylisted transport breaks ID generation. Also: an empty denylist must still allow loopback (tests and on-prem setups) and allowed public targets/redirects within MaxRedirects must keep working.
